raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not like taking big risks. On my 7 mu, I will still do wheat followed by maize, same as usual. This land has fed my family for many years, and with only 3 people at home I need a steady plan, not anything fancy. The well is useful, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times unless the weather turns dry. For wheat, I will sow in early October with a common improved variety people around here use. I usually put most fertilizer before sowing, then add some urea at jointing if the leaves are not strong enough. Wheat cannot be short of water at overwintering, jointing, and filling, but I will watch the rain and save one irrigation if the season is wet. After wheat harvest in June, the time is tight, so for maize I will not do heavy tillage. I will clear the straw and make a simple seedbed quickly so I can plant on time. Maize grows fast in summer, so if there is good rain I will save irrigation money, but if it stays dry around tasseling I will water once. I do not want to spend too much, but I also do not dare cut fertilizer too hard because if yield falls, that loss is bigger than saving a little cash.
